claims.quote: Insurers shall respond to any such supplemental requests as may be made within the timeframe and in the manner specified by Treasury.
claims.summary: Insurers must respond to any supplemental requests made by Treasury within the timeframe and in the manner specified.

claims.quote: The Secretary may collect information relating to small insurers, as defined in § 50.4(z), in order to conduct a study of small insurers participating in the Program, and identify any competitive challenges small insurers face in the terrorism risk insurance marketplace.
claims.summary: The Secretary may collect information relating to small insurers to conduct a study of small insurers participating in the Program and identify competitive challenges they face.

claims.quote: Information collected concerning small insurers may include information necessary for Treasury to identify: (1) Changes to the market share, premium volume, and policyholder surplus of small insurers relative to large insurers; (2) How the property and casualty insurance market for terrorism risk differs between small and large insurers, and whether such a difference exists within other perils; (3) The impact on small insurers of the Program's mandatory availability requirement under section 103(c) of the Act; (4) The effect on small insurers of increasing the trigger amount for the Program under section 103(e)(1)(B) of the Act; (5) The availability and cost of private reinsurance for small insurers; and (6) The impact that state workers compensation laws have on small insurers and workers compensation carriers in the terrorism risk insurance marketplace.
claims.summary: Information collected concerning small insurers may include details necessary for Treasury to identify changes in market share, premium volume, and policyholder surplus, differences in the insurance market, impact of the Program's requirements, availability and cost of reinsurance, and the impact of state workers compensation laws.

claims.quote: Subsequent to any certification by the Secretary of an act of terrorism, insurers shall report to Treasury information respecting insured losses arising from the act of terrorism.
claims.summary: Insurers must report to Treasury information regarding insured losses arising from an act of terrorism.

claims.quote: Reporting under this subsection shall be by a form prescribed by Treasury and made available on the Treasury Web site, which provides basic information about each claim established by an insurer that involves or potentially involves an insured loss.
claims.summary: Insurers must report using a form prescribed by Treasury and made available on the Treasury Web site.

claims.quote: Information to be reported for any claims by or against a policyholder shall identify paid and reserved amounts associated with the claim.
claims.summary: Insurers must identify paid and reserved amounts associated with claims.

claims.quote: In the case of an affiliated group of insurers, the form required by this subsection shall be submitted by a single insurer designated within the affiliated group, which shall report on a consolidated basis.
claims.summary: An affiliated group of insurers must submit a single report on a consolidated basis.

claims.quote: Data and information reported under this subsection will include: (1) A listing of each claim by name of insured, catastrophe code, line of business, and in the case of an affiliated group of insurers, the particular insurer or insurers within the group associated with each claim;
claims.summary: Insurers must include a listing of each claim by name of insured, catastrophe code, line of business, and the particular insurer or insurers within the group associated with each claim.

claims.quote: (2) Amounts paid, both loss and loss adjustment expenses, in connection with the claim as of the effective date of the report; and (3) Amounts reserved, both loss and loss adjustment expenses, in connection with the claim as of the effective date of the report.
claims.summary: Insurers must report amounts paid and reserved, both loss and loss adjustment expenses, in connection with the claim as of the effective date of the report.

claims.quote: To the extent that an insurer has established one or more claims that it believes involve insured losses arising from an act of terrorism, the insurer shall submit its first report within 60 days of establishing the first of such claims. An updated report shall be submitted each month thereafter, reporting data as of the prior month, until all claims arising from the act of terrorism have been resolved.
claims.summary: Insurers must submit their first report within 60 days of establishing the first claim involving insured losses from an act of terrorism and submit updated reports monthly until all such claims are resolved.

claims.quote: An insurer subject to such a data call shall respond to this request within the time frame specified in the request.
claims.summary: Insurers must respond to data requests from Treasury within the time frame specified in the request.

claims.quote: All nonpublic information submitted to the Secretary under subparts F and G of this part shall be considered proprietary information and shall: (1) Be handled and stored by Treasury in an appropriately secure manner; (2) Be considered, where appropriate, to be trade secrets or commercial or financial information obtained from a person and privileged or confidential; and (3) Not be publicly released in any unaggregated form in which a consumer, policyholder, or insurer is identifiable.
claims.affected_party: parties submitting nonpublic information under subparts F and G
claims.summary: Nonpublic information submitted under subparts F and G must be handled securely, considered as trade secrets or confidential information, and not publicly released in any unaggregated form that identifies individuals.

claims.quote: To the extent Treasury utilizes an insurance statistical aggregator in connection with any data collection under subparts F and G, such insurance statistical aggregator shall keep any nonpublic information that it collects confidential, consistent with the requirements of this section.
claims.summary: Insurance statistical aggregators must keep nonpublic information confidential when used by Treasury for data collection under subparts F and G.

claims.quote: The submission of any non-publicly available data and information to the Secretary under subparts F and G of this part, and the sharing of any non-publicly available data with or by the Secretary among other Federal agencies, the state insurance regulatory authorities, or any other entities shall not constitute a waiver of, or otherwise affect, any privilege or immunity arising under Federal or state law (including the rules of any Federal or state court) to which the data or information is otherwise subject.
claims.affected_party: parties submitting non-publicly available data and information under subparts F and G
claims.summary: Submission or sharing of non-publicly available data and information under subparts F and G shall not affect any privilege or immunity under Federal or state law.

claims.quote: Any requirement under Federal or state law to the extent otherwise applicable, or any requirement pursuant to a written agreement in effect between the original source of any non-publicly available data or information and the source of such data or information to the Secretary, regarding privacy or confidentiality of any data or information in the possession of the source to the Secretary, shall continue to apply to such data or information after the data or information has been provided pursuant to this subpart.
claims.affected_party: original source of non-publicly available data or information
claims.summary: Requirements under Federal or state law or written agreements regarding privacy or confidentiality of data or information shall continue to apply after the data or information has been provided to the Secretary under this subpart.

claims.quote: Section 552 of title 5, United States Code, including any exceptions thereunder, shall apply to any data or information submitted under this Subpart by an insurer or affiliate of an insurer.
claims.affected_party: insurer or affiliate of an insurer
claims.summary: Section 552 of title 5, United States Code, including any exceptions, shall apply to any data or information submitted under this subpart.

claims.quote: The Secretary, in consultation with the Attorney General of the United States and the Secretary of Homeland Security, is responsible for determining whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism.
claims.summary: The Secretary, in consultation with the Attorney General of the United States and the Secretary of Homeland Security, is responsible for determining whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism.

claims.quote: The Secretary's review finds that the act satisfies the elements for certification under § 50.4(b)(1)(i) through (iv), and that it is not otherwise precluded from certification by
claims.summary: The Secretary's review must find that the act satisfies the elements for certification under § 50.4(b)(1)(i) through (iv) and is not otherwise precluded from certification.

claims.quote: Within 30 days or as soon as otherwise practicable after the review identified in paragraph (b)(3) of this section concludes that the act satisfies the necessary criteria, the Secretary consults with the Attorney General of the United States and the Secretary of Homeland Security pursuant to section 102(1)(A) of the Act.
claims.summary: The Secretary must consult with the Attorney General of the United States and the Secretary of Homeland Security within 30 days or as soon as otherwise practicable after the review concludes that the act satisfies the necessary criteria.

claims.quote: Treasury shall publish a notice in the Federal Register within 30 days of the Secretary commencing review notifying the public that the act is under review for certification as an act of terrorism.
claims.summary: Treasury must publish a notice in the Federal Register within 30 days of the Secretary commencing review to notify the public that the act is under review for certification as an act of terrorism.

claims.quote: Not later than 30 days following the publication of a notice under paragraph (a) of this section that an act is under review for certification, and not later than every 60 days thereafter until the Secretary determines whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism, Treasury shall publish a notice in the Federal Register notifying the public whether the act is still under review for certification as an act of terrorism.
claims.summary: Treasury must publish a notice in the Federal Register not later than 30 days following the publication of a notice under paragraph (a) of this section that an act is under review for certification, and not later than every 60 days thereafter until the Secretary determines whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism.

claims.quote: If, in the discretion of the Secretary, circumstances relating to an act render timely notification under this section by Treasury impracticable, Treasury shall provide the notification as soon as practicable, in a manner the Secretary determines is appropriate.
claims.summary: If circumstances relating to an act render timely notification under this section by Treasury impracticable, Treasury must provide the notification as soon as practicable, in a manner the Secretary determines is appropriate.

claims.quote: The information sought by the Secretary shall be specified in the data request, and any insurer subject to the data request shall respond to the request within the time frame specified by the Secretary at the time of the request.
claims.summary: An insurer subject to a data request must respond to the request within the time frame specified by the Secretary.

claims.quote: Not later than 5 business days after the Secretary determines whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism, Treasury shall publish a statement and submit a notice to the Federal Register notifying the public of the Secretary's decision.
claims.summary: Treasury must publish a statement and submit a notice to the Federal Register within 5 business days of determining whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism.

claims.quote: Not later than 5 business days after the Secretary determines whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism, Treasury shall notify in writing any relevant supervisory officials of the Secretary's decision.
claims.summary: Treasury must notify relevant supervisory officials in writing within 5 business days of determining whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism.

claims.quote: Not later than 5 business days after the Secretary determines whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism, Treasury shall notify in writing the President of the U.S. Senate and the Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives of the Secretary's decision.
claims.summary: Treasury must notify the President of the U.S. Senate and the Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives in writing within 5 business days of determining whether to certify an act as an act of terrorism.

claims.quote: Treasury will pay the Federal share of compensation for insured losses as provided in section 103 of the Act once a Certification of Loss required by
claims.summary: Treasury must pay the Federal share of compensation for insured losses once a Certification of Loss is deemed sufficient.

claims.quote: The percentages in paragraph (a)(1) of this section are subject to any adjustments described in
claims.summary: The percentages for the Federal share of compensation are subject to adjustments described in the referenced section.

claims.quote: Federal compensation will not be paid by Treasury unless the aggregate industry insured losses resulting from one or more certified acts of terrorism exceed the following amounts: (1) For insured losses resulting from acts of terrorism taking place in calendar year 2015: $100 million; (2) For insured losses resulting from acts of terrorism taking place in calendar year 2016: $120 million; (3) For insured losses resulting from acts of terrorism taking place in calendar year 2017: $140 million; (4) For insured losses resulting from acts of terrorism taking place in calendar year 2018: $160 million; (5) For insured losses resulting from acts of terrorism taking place in calendar year 2019: $180 million; (6) For insured losses resulting from acts of terrorism taking place in calendar year 2020 and any calendar year thereafter: $200 million.
claims.summary: Federal compensation will not be paid unless the aggregate industry insured losses from certified acts of terrorism exceed specified amounts for each calendar year.

claims.quote: Treasury shall pay the appropriate amount of the Federal share of compensation for an insured loss to an insurer upon a determination that: (1) The insurer is an entity, including an affiliate thereof, that meets the requirements of § 50.4(o); (2) The insurer's insured losses, as defined in § 50.4(n) and limited by paragraph (d) of this section (including the allocated dollar value of the insurer's proportionate share of insured losses from a state residual market insurance entity or a state workers' compensation fund as described in § 5.33), have exceeded its insurer deductible as defined in § 50.4(p); (3) The insurer has paid or is prepared to pay an insured loss, based on a filed claim for the insured loss; (4) Neither the insurer's claim for Federal payment nor any underlying claim for an insured loss is fraudulent, collusive, made in bad faith, dishonest or otherwise designed to circumvent the purposes of the Act and regulations; (5) The insurer has provided a clear and conspicuous disclosure as required by §§ 50.10 through 50.14 and a cap disclosure as required by § 50.15; (6) The insurer offered coverage for insured losses and the offer was accepted by the insured prior to the act which results in the insured loss; (7) The insurer took all steps reasonably necessary to properly and carefully investigate the insured loss and otherwise processed the insured loss using practices appropriate for the business of insurance; (8) The insured loss is within the scope of coverage issued by the insurer under the terms and conditions of one or more policies for commercial property and casualty insurance as defined in § 50.4(w); and (9) The procedures specified in this Subpart have been followed and all conditions for payment have been met.
claims.summary: Treasury shall pay the Federal share of compensation for an insured loss to an insurer upon a determination that the insurer meets all specified conditions, including providing clear and conspicuous disclosure, offering coverage, and following procedures.

claims.quote: Treasury may subsequently adjust, including requiring repayment of, any payment made under paragraph (c) of this section in accordance with its authority under the Act.
claims.summary: Treasury may adjust or require repayment of any payment made under paragraph (c) of this section in accordance with its authority under the Act.

claims.quote: Upon a determination by Treasury that an insurer has failed to meet any of the requirements for payment specified in paragraph (c) of this section for a particular insured loss, Treasury may suspend payment of the Federal share of compensation for all other insured losses of the insurer pending investigation and audit of the insurer's insured losses.
claims.summary: Treasury may suspend payment of the Federal share of compensation for all other insured losses of an insurer if it determines the insurer has failed to meet any of the requirements for payment specified in paragraph (c) of this section.

claims.quote: Treasury will determine the amount of aggregate industry insured losses resulting from a certified act of terrorism. If aggregate industry insured losses in a calendar year resulting from one or more certified acts of terrorism exceed the applicable Program Trigger amounts specified in paragraph (b) of this section, Treasury will publish a document in the Federal Register of a Program Trigger Event.
claims.summary: Treasury will determine the amount of aggregate industry insured losses resulting from a certified act of terrorism and will publish a document in the Federal Register of a Program Trigger Event if the losses exceed the applicable Program Trigger amounts.

claims.quote: The aggregate amount of insured losses of an insurer in a calendar year used to calculate the Federal share of compensation shall be reduced by any amounts recovered by the insurer as salvage or subrogation for its insured losses in the calendar year.
claims.summary: The insurer must reduce the aggregate amount of insured losses by any amounts recovered as salvage or subrogation.

claims.quote: The sum of the Federal share of compensation paid by Treasury to an insurer and the insurer's recoveries for insured losses from other sources shall not be greater than the insurer's aggregate amount of insured losses for acts of terrorism in that calendar year.
claims.summary: The insurer must ensure that the sum of the Federal share of compensation and recoveries from other sources does not exceed the insurer's aggregate amount of insured losses for acts of terrorism.

claims.quote: Amounts recovered for insured losses in excess of an insurer's aggregate amount of insured losses for acts of terrorism in a calendar year shall be repaid to Treasury within 45 days after the end of the month in which total recoveries of the insurer, from all sources, become excess.
claims.summary: The insurer must repay any excess recoveries to Treasury within 45 days after the end of the month in which total recoveries become excess.

claims.quote: The Federal share of compensation for insured losses under the Program shall be reduced by the amount of other compensation provided by other Federal programs to an insured or a third party to the extent such other compensation duplicates the insurance indemnification for those insured losses.
claims.summary: The Federal share of compensation must be reduced by the amount of other compensation provided by other Federal programs that duplicates insurance indemnification for insured losses.

claims.quote: With respect to any underlying claim for insured losses, each insurer shall inquire of all involved policyholders, insureds, and claimants whether the person receiving insurance proceeds for an insured loss has received, expects to receive, or is entitled to receive compensation from another Federal program for the insured loss, and if so, the source and the amount of the compensation received or expected.
claims.summary: Each insurer must inquire about whether the person receiving insurance proceeds has received or is entitled to receive compensation from another Federal program for the insured loss.

claims.quote: The response, source, and such amounts shall be reported with each underlying claim on the form specified in § 50.73(b)(1).
claims.summary: The insurer must report the response, source, and amounts of compensation received or expected from another Federal program with each underlying claim on the specified form.

claims.quote: Each insurer shall submit to Treasury a Notice on a form prescribed by Treasury whenever the insurer's aggregate insured losses (including reserves for “incurred but not reported” losses) within a calendar year exceed an amount equal to 50 percent of the insurer's deductible as specified in § 50.4(p).
claims.summary: The insurer must submit a Notice to Treasury on a prescribed form whenever the insurer's aggregate insured losses exceed 50 percent of the deductible as specified in § 50.4(p).

claims.quote: In the case of an affiliated group of insurers, the Notice will include the name and address of a single designated insurer within the affiliated group that will serve as the single point of contact for the purpose of providing loss and compliance certifications as required in § 50.73 and for receiving, disbursing, and distributing payments of the Federal share of compensation in accordance with
claims.summary: In the case of an affiliated group of insurers, the Notice must include the name and address of a single designated insurer to serve as the single point of contact for providing loss and compliance certifications and for receiving, disbursing, and distributing payments of the Federal share of compensation.

claims.quote: The insurer shall file an Initial Certification of Loss, on a form prescribed by Treasury, and thereafter such Supplementary Certifications of Loss, on a form prescribed by Treasury, as may be necessary to receive payment for the Federal share of compensation for its insured losses.
claims.summary: The insurer must file an Initial Certification of Loss and any necessary Supplementary Certifications of Loss to receive payment for the Federal share of compensation for its insured losses.

claims.quote: An insurer shall use its best efforts to file with the Program the Initial Certification of Loss within 45 days following the last calendar day of the month when an insurer has paid aggregate insured losses that exceed its insurer deductible.
claims.summary: The insurer must use its best efforts to file the Initial Certification of Loss within 45 days after the last calendar day of the month when aggregate insured losses exceed its insurer deductible.

claims.quote: The Initial Certification of Loss will include the following: (1) Basic information, on a form prescribed by Treasury, about each insured loss paid (or to be paid pursuant to § 50.73(b)(2)(i)) by the insurer. The form will include: (i) A listing of each insured loss paid (or to be paid pursuant to § 50.73(b)(2)(i)) by the insurer by catastrophe code and line of business; (ii) The total amount of reinsurance recovered from other sources; (iii) A calculation of the aggregate insured losses sustained by the insurer above its insurer deductible for the calendar year; and (iv) The amount the insurer claims as the Federal share of compensation for its aggregate insured losses.
claims.summary: The Initial Certification of Loss must include basic information about each insured loss paid or to be paid, a listing by catastrophe code and line of business, total reinsurance recovered, a calculation of aggregate insured losses above the insurer deductible, and the amount claimed as the Federal share of compensation.

claims.quote: (2) A certification that the insurer is in compliance with the provisions of section 103(b) of the Act and this part, including certifications that: (i) The underlying insured losses reported pursuant to § 50.73(b)(1) either: Have been paid by the insurer; or will be paid by the insurer upon receipt of an advance payment of the Federal share of compensation as soon as possible, consistent with the insurer's normal business practices, but not longer than five business days after receipt of the Federal share of compensation; (ii) The underlying claims for insured losses were filed by persons who suffered an insured loss, or by persons acting on behalf of such persons; (iii) The underlying claims for insured losses were processed in accordance with appropriate business practices and the procedures specified in this subpart; (iv) The insurer has complied with the disclosure requirements of §§ 50.10 through 50.14, and the cap disclosure requirement of § 50.15, for each underlying insured loss that is included in the amount of the insurer's aggregate insured losses; and (v) The insurer has complied with the mandatory availability requirements of subpart C of this part.
claims.summary: The insurer must certify compliance with section 103(b) of the Act and this part, including that underlying insured losses are paid or will be paid within five business days, claims were filed by persons who suffered a loss or their representatives, claims were processed in accordance with business practices and procedures, disclosure requirements were met, and mandatory availability requirements were met.

claims.quote: (3) A certification of the amount of the insurer's direct earned premium, together with the calculation of its insurer deductible (provided this certification was not submitted previously with the Notice of Deductible Erosion).
claims.summary: The insurer must certify the amount of its direct earned premium and the calculation of its insurer deductible, provided this certification was not previously submitted with the Notice of Deductible Erosion.

claims.quote: (4) A certification that the insurer will disburse payment of the Federal share of compensation in accordance with this Subpart.
claims.summary: The insurer must certify that it will disburse payment of the Federal share of compensation in accordance with this Subpart.

claims.quote: (5) A certification that if Treasury has determined a Pro Rata Loss Percentage (PRLP) (see § 50.112), the insurer has complied with applying the PRLP to insured loss payments, where required.
claims.summary: The insurer must certify that it has complied with applying the Pro Rata Loss Percentage (PRLP) to insured loss payments, where required.

claims.quote: If the total amount of the Federal share of compensation due an insurer for insured losses under the Act has not been determined at the time an Initial Certification of Loss has been filed, the insurer shall file monthly, or on a schedule otherwise determined by Treasury, Supplementary Certifications of Loss updating the amount of the Federal share of compensation due for the insurer's insured losses.
claims.summary: The insurer must file monthly or on a schedule determined by Treasury, Supplementary Certifications of Loss to update the amount of the Federal share of compensation due for its insured losses if the total amount has not been determined at the time of the Initial Certification of Loss.

claims.quote: Supplementary Certifications of Loss will include the following: (1) A form as described in
claims.summary: Supplementary Certifications of Loss will include a form as described in the relevant section.

claims.quote: A certification as described in § 50.73(b)(2).
claims.summary: An insurer must provide a certification as described in § 50.73(b)(2).

claims.quote: Treasury may require such additional supporting documentation as required to ascertain the Federal share of compensation for the insured losses of any insurer.
claims.summary: Treasury may require additional supporting documentation to ascertain the Federal share of compensation for the insured losses of any insurer.

claims.quote: A state residual market insurance entity or a state workers' compensation fund described in § 50.32 shall provide the Certifications of Loss described in § 50.73(b) and (c) for all of its insured losses to each participating insurer at the time it provides the allocated dollar value of the participating insurer's proportionate share of insured losses.
claims.affected_party: state residual market insurance entity or state workers' compensation fund
claims.summary: A state residual market insurance entity or a state workers' compensation fund must provide the Certifications of Loss described in § 50.73(b) and (c) for all of its insured losses to each participating insurer at the time it provides the allocated dollar value of the participating insurer's proportionate share of insured losses.

claims.quote: In addition, at such time the state residual market insurance entity or state workers' compensation fund shall provide the certification described in § 50.73(b)(2) to Treasury.
claims.affected_party: state residual market insurance entity or state workers' compensation fund
claims.summary: At such time, the state residual market insurance entity or state workers' compensation fund must provide the certification described in § 50,73(b)(2) to Treasury.

claims.quote: An insurer that requests payment of the Federal Share of Compensation for insured losses must receive payment through electronic funds transfer.
claims.summary: An insurer that requests payment of the Federal Share of Compensation for insured losses must receive payment through electronic funds transfer.

claims.quote: An insurer shall designate an account for the receipt of reimbursement of the Federal share of compensation at an institution eligible to receive payments through the Automated Clearing House (ACH) network.
claims.summary: An insurer shall designate an account for the receipt of reimbursement of the Federal share of compensation at an institution eligible to receive payments through the Automated Clearing House (ACH) network.

claims.quote: An insurer that seeks advance payments of the Federal share of compensation as certified according to
claims.summary: An insurer that seeks advance payments of the Federal share of compensation as certified according to...

claims.quote: All interest earned on advance payments in the segregated account must be remitted at least quarterly to Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service or as otherwise prescribed in applicable procedures.
claims.summary: The insurer must remit interest earned on advance payments in the segregated account at least quarterly to Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service.

claims.quote: Treasury may deny or withhold advance payments of the Federal share of compensation to an insurer if Treasury determines that the insurer has not properly disbursed previous advances of the Federal share of compensation or otherwise has not complied with the requirements for advance payment as provided in this Subpart.
claims.summary: Treasury may deny or withhold advance payments if the insurer has not properly disbursed previous advances or has not complied with the requirements for advance payment.

claims.quote: The designated insurer receiving payment from Treasury must distribute payment to affiliated insurers in a manner that ensures that each insurer in the affiliated group is compensated for its share of insured losses, taking into account a reasonable and fair allocation of the group deductible among affiliated insurers.
claims.summary: The designated insurer must distribute payment to affiliated insurers in a manner that ensures each insurer is compensated for its share of insured losses, with a reasonable and fair allocation of the group deductible.

claims.quote: The Secretary may determine a Final Netting Date for a calendar year, which for purposes of this part is the date on or before which an insurer must report to Treasury on the insurer's Certifications of Loss (both Initial Certification of Loss and any Supplemental Certifications of Loss) all insured losses that have been reported by its policyholders for the calendar year.
claims.summary: The insurer must report to Treasury on the insurer's Certifications of Loss all insured losses reported by its policyholders for the calendar year on or before the Final Netting Date.

claims.quote: Treasury shall announce and publish in the Federal Register notice of a proposed Final Netting Date and its application to a specific calendar year, and will solicit comments from the public regarding the appropriateness of the proposed Final Netting Date.
claims.summary: Treasury must announce and publish a proposed Final Netting Date and solicit public comments.

claims.quote: After receipt and evaluation of comments respecting its proposed Final Netting Date, Treasury will publish in the Federal Register a Final Netting Date, which is at least 180 days after the date of publication.
claims.summary: Treasury must publish a Final Netting Date at least 180 days after the date of publication.

claims.quote: An insurer may not report any new underlying insured losses, or increased workers' compensation loss amounts based on an increase in the number of workers' compensation claimants, to Treasury after a Final Netting Date, except as provided in this section.
claims.summary: Insurers may not report new underlying insured losses or increased workers' compensation loss amounts after a Final Netting Date, except as provided.

claims.quote: The payment by Treasury of a final commuted amount to an insurer will discharge Treasury from all future liabilities to the insurer for the Federal share of compensation for insured losses for the applicable calendar year.
claims.summary: Treasury must pay a final commuted amount to discharge all future liabilities for the Federal share of compensation for insured losses.

claims.quote: payment of the final commuted amount to the designated insurer of the affiliated group discharges Treasury's payment obligation to the insurers in the affiliated group for insured losses for the applicable calendar year.
claims.summary: The insurer must pay the final commuted amount to the designated insurer of the affiliated group to discharge Treasury's payment obligation for insured losses.

claims.quote: Insurers will be required to justify discount and other factors from which final payment amounts are derived.
claims.summary: Insurers must justify discount and other factors used to derive final payment amounts.

claims.quote: If the insurer fails to provide the requested information, it will forfeit the right to future payments from Treasury.
claims.summary: Insurers must provide requested information; otherwise, they forfeit the right to future payments from Treasury.

claims.quote: Payments of commuted amounts are not considered to be advance payments requiring a segregated account as described in § 50.74(d).
claims.summary: Payments of commuted amounts are not considered advance payments requiring a segregated account.

claims.quote: a payment by Treasury of a final commuted amount to an insurer is final unless: (i) Treasury is put on notice that an insurer's claim was fraudulent or that other conditions for Federal payment were not met, in which case the insurer will be required to repay amounts that were not due; or (ii) The exception in paragraph (e) of this section applies, in which case Treasury may make additional payments for insured losses, but only under the conditions described in paragraph (e).
claims.summary: A payment by Treasury of a final commuted amount to an insurer is final unless the insurer's claim is fraudulent or other conditions for Federal payment are not met, in which case the insurer must repay amounts that were not due.

claims.quote: The Secretary of the Treasury, or an authorized representative, shall have, upon reasonable notice, access to all books, documents, papers and records of an insurer that are pertinent to amounts paid to the insurer as the Federal share of compensation for insured losses, or pertinent to any Federal terrorism policy surcharge that is imposed pursuant to subpart J of this part, for the purposes of investigation, confirmation, audit, and examination.
claims.summary: The Secretary of the Treasury or an authorized representative must have access to all pertinent books, documents, papers, and records of an insurer for the purposes of investigation, confirmation, audit, and examination.

claims.quote: Each insurer that seeks payment of a Federal share of compensation under subpart H of this part shall retain such records as are necessary to fully disclose all material matters pertinent to insured losses and the Federal share of compensation sought under the Program, including, but not limited to, records regarding premiums and insured losses for all commercial property and casualty insurance issued by the insurer and information relating to any adjustment in the amount of the Federal share of compensation payable. Insurers shall maintain detailed records for not less than five (5) years from the termination dates of all reinsurance agreements involving property and casualty insurance subject to the Act. Records relating to premiums shall be retained and available for review for not less than three (3) years following the conclusion of the policy year. Records relating to underlying claims shall be retained for not less than five (5) years following the final adjustment of the claim.
claims.summary: Insurers must retain records related to insured losses, Federal share of compensation, premiums, reinsurance agreements, and underlying claims for specified periods.

claims.quote: Each insurer that collects a Federal terrorism policy surcharge as required by subpart J of this part shall retain records related to such surcharge, including records of the property and casualty insurance premiums subject to the surcharge, the amount of the surcharge imposed on each policy, aggregate Federal terrorism policy surcharges collected, and aggregate Federal terrorism policy surcharges remitted to Treasury during each assessment period. Such records shall be retained and kept available for review for not less than three (3) years following the conclusion of the assessment period or settlement of accounts with Treasury, whichever is later.
claims.summary: Insurers must retain records related to Federal terrorism policy surcharge, including premiums, surcharge amounts, and aggregate surcharges, for a minimum of three years.

claims.quote: The Secretary may assess a civil monetary penalty, in an amount not exceeding the amount specified under § 50.83, against any insurer that the Secretary determines, on the record after opportunity for a hearing: (1) Has failed to charge, collect, or remit the Federal terrorism policy surcharge under subpart J; (2) Has intentionally provided to Treasury erroneous information regarding premium or loss amounts; (3) Submits to Treasury fraudulent claims under the Program for insured losses; (4) Has failed to provide any disclosures or other information required by Treasury; or (5) Has otherwise failed to comply with provisions of the Act or these regulations.
claims.summary: The Secretary may assess civil monetary penalties against insurers for failing to charge, collect, or remit the Federal terrorism policy surcharge, providing erroneous information, submitting fraudulent claims, failing to provide required disclosures, or otherwise failing to comply with the Act or regulations.

claims.quote: A penalty under this section for any failure to pay, charge, collect, or remit amounts in accordance with the Act or under these regulations shall be in addition to any such amounts recovered by Treasury.
claims.summary: Penalties for failure to pay, charge, collect, or remit amounts under the Act or regulations are in addition to any amounts recovered by Treasury.

claims.quote: Treasury shall notify in writing any insurer that it believes has committed one or more of the acts identified in paragraph (a) of this section. In that notification, Treasury shall identify the act or acts that it believes has been violated, and its basis for that belief, and shall set a schedule for further proceedings which shall include: (1) The opportunity for a written submission by the insurer that provides all relevant facts and circumstances concerning the alleged conduct, including any information that the insurer wishes Treasury to consider in connection with the alleged conduct; and (2) A hearing on the record, unless waived by the insurer, during which Treasury and the insurer may present further information respecting the conduct in question.
claims.summary: Treasury must notify insurers in writing of alleged violations, provide an opportunity for written submission, and set a schedule for a hearing on the record unless waived by the insurer.

claims.quote: Treasury's assessment and collection of a civil monetary penalty under this section shall be in addition and without prejudice to any other civil remedies or criminal penalties that may arise on account of the conduct in question under any other laws or regulations of the United States.
claims.summary: Assessment and collection of civil monetary penalties under this section are in addition to and without prejudice to other civil remedies or criminal penalties under other laws or regulations.

claims.quote: Any penalty under the Act and these regulations may not exceed the greater of $1,741,100 and, in the case of any failure to pay, charge, collect or remit amounts in accordance with the Act or these regulations such amount in dispute.
claims.affected_party: any party subject to the Act and these regulations
claims.summary: Penalties under the Act and these regulations may not exceed the greater of $1,741,100 or the amount in dispute for failure to pay, charge, collect, or remit amounts.

claims.quote: The maximum penalty amount that may be assessed under this section will be adjusted in accordance with the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act Improvements Act of 2015, 28 U.S.C. 2461 note, by January 15 of each year and the updated amount will be posted in the Federal Register and on the Treasury website at https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/financial-markets-financial-institutions-and-fiscal-service/federal-insurance-office/terrorism-risk-insurance-program.
claims.summary: The maximum penalty amount under this section will be adjusted annually by January 15 and the updated amount will be posted in the Federal Register and on the Treasury website.

claims.quote: The Secretary shall impose, and insurers shall collect, such Federal terrorism policy surcharges as needed to recover 140 percent of the mandatory recoupment amount for any calendar year.
claims.summary: The Secretary shall impose and insurers shall collect Federal terrorism policy surcharges as needed to recover 140 percent of the mandatory recoupment amount for any calendar year.

claims.quote: The Secretary may recover any portion of the aggregate Federal share of compensation that exceeds the mandatory recoupment amount through a Federal terrorism policy surcharge based on the factors set forth in section 103(e)(7)(D) of the Act.
claims.summary: The Secretary may recover any portion of the aggregate Federal share of compensation exceeding the mandatory recoupment amount through a Federal terrorism policy surcharge based on the factors in section 103(e)(7)(D) of the Act.

claims.quote: If the Secretary imposes a federal terrorism policy surcharge as provided in paragraph (a) of this section, then the required amounts, based upon the extent to which payments for the Federal Share of Compensation have been made by the collection deadlines in section 103(e)(7)(E) of the Act, shall be collected in accordance with such deadlines: (1) For any act of terrorism that occurs on or before December 31, 2022, the Secretary shall collect all required amounts by September 30, 2024; (2) For any act of terrorism that occurs between January 1, 2023 and December 31, 2023, the Secretary shall collect 35% of any required amounts by September 30, 2024, and the remainder by September 30, 2029; and (3) For any act of terrorism that occurs on or after January 1, 2024, the Secretary shall collect all required amounts by September 30, 2029.
claims.summary: The Secretary shall collect required amounts for Federal Share of Compensation in accordance with specific deadlines based on the date of the act of terrorism.

claims.quote: If payments for the Federal share of compensation have been made for a calendar year, and Treasury determines that insured loss information is sufficiently developed and credible to serve as a basis for calculating recoupment amounts, Treasury will make an initial determination of any mandatory or discretionary recoupment amounts for that calendar year.
claims.summary: Treasury must make an initial determination of any mandatory or discretionary recoupment amounts for a calendar year if payments for the Federal share of compensation have been made and insured loss information is sufficiently developed and credible.

claims.quote: Within 90 days after certification of an act of terrorism, the Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register an estimate of aggregate insured losses which shall be used as the basis for initially determining whether mandatory recoupment will be required.
claims.summary: The Secretary must publish in the Federal Register an estimate of aggregate insured losses within 90 days after certification of an act of terrorism.

claims.quote: If at any time Treasury projects that payments for the Federal share of compensation will be made for a calendar year, and that in order to meet the collection timing requirements of section 103(e)(7)(E) of the Act it is necessary to use an estimate of such payments as a basis for calculating recoupment amounts, Treasury will make an initial determination of any mandatory recoupment amounts for that calendar year.
claims.summary: Treasury must make an initial determination of any mandatory recoupment amounts for a calendar year if it projects that payments for the Federal share of compensation will be made and an estimate is necessary to meet collection timing requirements.

claims.quote: Following the initial determination of recoupment amounts for a calendar year, Treasury will recalculate any mandatory or discretionary recoupment amount as necessary and appropriate, and at least annually, until a final recoupment amount for the calendar year is determined.
claims.summary: Treasury must recalculate any mandatory or discretionary recoupment amount as necessary and appropriate, at least annually, until a final recoupment amount for the calendar year is determined.

claims.quote: Treasury will compare any recalculated recoupment amount to amounts already remitted and/or to be remitted to Treasury for a Federal terrorism policy surcharge previously established to determine whether any additional amount will be recouped by Treasury.
claims.summary: Treasury must compare any recalculated recoupment amount to amounts already remitted and/or to be remitted to Treasury for a Federal terrorism policy surcharge previously established to determine whether any additional amount will be recouped.

claims.quote: For the purpose of determining initial or recalculated recoupment amounts, Treasury may issue a data call to insurers for insurer deductible and insured loss information by calendar year.
claims.summary: Treasury must issue a data call to insurers for insurer deductible and insured loss information by calendar year to determine initial or recalculated recoupment amounts.

claims.quote: Submission of data in response to a data call shall be on a form promulgated by Treasury.
claims.summary: Insurers must submit data in response to a data call on a form promulgated by Treasury.

claims.quote: The Federal terrorism policy surcharge shall be the obligation of the policyholder and is payable to the insurer with the premium for a property and casualty insurance policy in effect during the assessment period established by Treasury.
claims.summary: The policyholder must pay the Federal terrorism policy surcharge to the insurer with the premium for a property and casualty insurance policy in effect during the assessment period established by Treasury.

claims.quote: Treasury will provide notifications of recoupment through publication of notices in the Federal Register or in another manner Treasury deems appropriate, based upon the circumstances of the certified act(s) of terrorism under consideration.
claims.summary: Treasury must provide notifications of recoupment through publication in the Federal Register or another appropriate manner.

claims.quote: Treasury will provide reasonable advance notice to insurers of any initial Federal terrorism policy surcharge effective date. This effective date shall be January 1 of the calendar year following publication of the notice, unless such date would not provide for sufficient notice of implementation while meeting the collection timing requirements of section 103(e)(8)(E) of the Act.
claims.summary: Treasury must provide reasonable advance notice to insurers of the initial Federal terrorism policy surcharge effective date.

claims.quote: Treasury will provide reasonable advance notice to insurers of any modification or cessation of the Federal terrorism policy surcharge.
claims.summary: Treasury must provide reasonable advance notice to insurers of any modification or cessation of the Federal terrorism policy surcharge.

claims.quote: Treasury will provide notification to insurers annually as to the continuation of the Federal terrorism policy surcharge.
claims.summary: Treasury must provide annual notification to insurers regarding the continuation of the Federal terrorism policy surcharge.

claims.quote: Insurers shall collect a Federal terrorism policy surcharge from policyholders as required by Treasury.
claims.summary: Insurers must collect a Federal terrorism policy surcharge from policyholders as required by Treasury.

claims.quote: Policies subject to the Federal terrorism policy surcharge are those for which direct written premium is reported on commercial lines of business on the NAIC's Exhibit of Premiums and Losses of the NAIC Annual Statement (commonly known as Statutory Page 14) as provided in § 50.4(w)(1), or equivalently reported.
claims.summary: Insurers must report direct written premium on commercial lines of business on the NAIC's Exhibit of Premiums and Losses of the NAIC Annual Statement (Statutory Page 14) or equivalently reported.

claims.quote: The surcharge shall be imposed and collected on a written premium basis for policies that become effective or renew during the assessment period. All new, renewal, mid-term, and audit premiums for a policy term are subject to the surcharge in effect on the policy term effective date.
claims.summary: Insurers must impose and collect the surcharge on a written premium basis for policies that become effective or renew during the assessment period.

claims.quote: A policyholder must pay the applicable Federal terrorism policy surcharge when due. The insurer shall have such rights and remedies to enforce the collection of the surcharge that are the equivalent to those that exist under applicable state or other law for nonpayment of premium.
claims.summary: Policyholders must pay the applicable Federal terrorism policy surcharge when due. Insurers must have rights and remedies equivalent to those under applicable state or other law for nonpayment of premium.

claims.quote: When an insurer returns an unearned premium, or otherwise refunds premium to a policyholder, it shall also return any Federal terrorism policy surcharge collected that is attributable to the refunded unearned premium.
claims.summary: Insurers must return any Federal terrorism policy surcharge collected that is attributable to the refunded unearned premium when returning unearned premium or refunding premium to a policyholder.

claims.quote: Each insurer shall report direct written premium and Federal terrorism policy surcharges to Treasury on a monthly and annual basis during the assessment period.
claims.summary: Insurers must report direct written premium and Federal terrorism policy surcharges to Treasury monthly and annually during the assessment period.
